---
title: "GSim Developing Features"
---

This page is for GDSFactory/`gsim` developers reviewing the Palace workflow pieces that OrPen SC PDK needs. It separates two `gsim` feature candidates from the surrounding context that makes the examples meaningful.

The baseline is `gdsfactory/gsim` `upstream/main` at `16f6ef6`. The local review branch is `arfiligol/gsim` `feature/gsim-palace-postprocessing-roles` at `1a3f48f`, with local working-tree edits still present. The text below describes that branch-local delta, not accepted upstream behavior.

## Development Classification

| Area | Owner | Status | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SGB input contract | `semantic_geometry_builder`, consumed by `gsim` | Context dependency | Optional Route A/B/C semantic sidecar for terminal plans, interface ownership, and physical-group identity. |
| Slurm HPC handoff package | `gsim` | Upstream candidate | Run-stage packaging API that prepares a Palace run folder, Slurm script, metadata, and archive without submitting a job. |
| Resolve/Results | `gsim` | Upstream candidate | Completed-run resolver and typed report layer for Palace outputs. |
| OrPen notebooks | `orpen-sc-pdk` | Consumer evidence | Public fixtures showing how the two `gsim` features are used from notebooks. |
| Palace and Slurm runtime | External | Out of scope | Solver execution and site scheduling stay outside these docs and outside OrPen ownership. |

## Feature Contracts

| Feature | Need | Native `gsim` upstream/main | Local branch delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Slurm HPC handoff package](capabilities/gsim-slurm-hpc-handoff-package.qmd) | Let notebooks prepare reviewable HPC run packages without submitting jobs or embedding site runtime behavior. | Simulation, mesh, and Palace config generation exist; there is no first-class Slurm handoff package or canonical run-folder model. | Adds handoff helpers, run-folder/run-stage models, archive manifests, Slurm script writers, and `PalaceSimBase` wrappers. |
| [Resolve/Results](capabilities/gsim-resolve-results.qmd) | Let notebooks point at a completed Palace run folder and fail loudly or display typed C-matrix, domain, surface, and convergence results. | A monolithic `results.py` helper exists; there is no run-folder resolver, source audit, or typed problem report pipeline. | Adds `resolve`, CSV/JSON loaders, derived result tables, typed result models, and report classes reached through `resolve_palace_result(...).load_report()`. |

## Design

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A["Public or private layout"] --> B["gsim mesh/config"]
    C["Optional SGB semantic sidecar"] --> B
    B --> D["Run-stage handoff package"]
    D --> E["External Palace execution"]
    E --> F["Completed run folder"]
    F --> G["resolve_palace_result"]
    G --> H["Typed report objects"]
    H --> I["Notebook display"]
```

SGB is only an input-contract path where layer names are not enough to preserve terminal/interface identity. The two `gsim` features under review are the run-stage handoff package and the completed-run Resolve/Results layer.

## Notebook Entry Points

| Notebook | Role | Preconditions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Public Electrostatic Workflow](docs/notebooks/public_electrostatic_workflow.ipynb) | Canonical consumer for handoff package generation and Resolve/Results review. | Result sections require a completed Palace run folder or `NOTEBOOK_ANALYSIS_RUN_ROOT`. |
| [Public Driven Workflow](docs/notebooks/public_driven_workflow.ipynb) | Driven problem consumer shape. | Requires completed solver outputs for report cells. |
| [Public Eigenmode Workflow](docs/notebooks/public_eigenmode_workflow.ipynb) | Eigenmode problem consumer shape. | Requires completed solver outputs for report cells. |
| [Martinis Ribbon Route A](sgb-notebooks/martinis2022_ribbon_route_a.ipynb) | SGB context example for thin-film semantic identity. | Does not prove a `gsim` runtime feature by itself. |
| [Martinis Ribbon Route B](sgb-notebooks/martinis2022_ribbon_route_b.ipynb) | SGB context example for conductor-shell semantic identity. | Does not prove a `gsim` runtime feature by itself. |
| [Martinis Ribbon Route C](sgb-notebooks/martinis2022_ribbon_route_c.ipynb) | SGB context example for volume-oriented semantic identity. | Does not prove a `gsim` runtime feature by itself. |

## Review Order

| Order | Review | Done when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Slurm HPC handoff package | A notebook can prepare a run folder, sbatch script, metadata sidecar, and archive without submitting a job. |
| 2 | Resolve/Results | A notebook can resolve a completed Palace run folder and display typed reports, failing loudly when required outputs are absent. |
| 3 | Public notebook evidence | OrPen notebooks demonstrate the two `gsim` features using public fixtures and explicit external-run prerequisites. |
